ByteDance is a technology company whose Traffic Infrastructure team builds global edge infrastructure platforms for scalable, reliable, and cost-effective edge services. The Graduate Software Engineer will help design, develop, operate, and troubleshoot cloud-native infrastructure components and collaborate with SRE, platform, and product teams while developing expertise in distributed systems, networking, and observability.

Responsibilities
Contribute to the design, development, and operation of infrastructure components for global edge PoPs (e.g., Kubernetes/control plane, virtualization/containers, Ingress/Gateway), with guidance from mentor engineers, focusing on performance, reliability, and security
Participate in the end-to-end delivery of cloud-native features — from requirements and implementation to testing and production rollout — while learning our engineering best practices
Help build observability and troubleshooting tooling (metrics/logs/tracing/profiling) and contribute to automation that improves incident response efficiency
Collaborate with SRE, platform, and product teams, and grow into an engineer who can independently own standardized, reusable platform capabilities for traffic-intensive services

Required
- Individuals who are currently pursuing or recently completed a BS/MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, graduating within the past year or by the expected start date
- Solid foundation in software engineering fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, operating systems, computer networks)
- Programming experience in one or more languages such as Go, C or Rust, demonstrated through coursework, personal projects, internships, or open-source contributions
- Familiarity with Linux and basic understanding of containers, distributed systems, or networking concepts
- Strong problem-solving skills, a growth mindset, ownership, and eagerness to learn in a collaborative, fast-paced environment
Preferred
- Internship, co-op, or research experience related to backend/systems development, cloud-native technologies, or infrastructure
- Hands-on exposure to containers and Kubernetes through coursework, side projects, or internships (e.g., deploying applications, basic cluster operations, service discovery, Ingress/Gateway)
- Contributions to cloud-native open-source projects (e.g., Kubernetes, Containerd, Cilium/eBPF), even at a small scale
- Deeper Linux knowledge (kernel, scheduling, TCP/IP, routing, iptables/nftables) gained through projects or self-study
- Coursework, projects, or curiosity around CDN, live streaming, RTC, or other edge/traffic-intensive architectures
